newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Meiling 96 net surges on increased sales.
newsitem.headline: Meiling 96 net surges on increased sales.

text.p: Hefei Meiling Co said on Tuesday that a surge in the firm's 1996 post-tax profit was due to increased sales on strong demand for refrigerators, its principal product.

Net profit for 1996 hit 138.3 million yuan in 1996, an increase of 45.47 percent from 95.1 million yuan in 1995 based on international accounting standards, the company said in its 1996 annual report published on Tuesday.
Based on domestic accounting standards, the 1996 net was 144.9438 million yuan against 112.41 million yuan in 1995.
Turnover rose 19.35 percent to 1,517.1789 million yuan in 1996 from 1,271.2 million yuan in 1995 based on domestic accounting standards, the report said.
Strong demand saw the company sell 99.6 percent of the 800,000 refrigerators it produced in 1996, the report said.

Meiling expects a further 10 percent rise in net profit in 1997, a company official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin on Tuesday. Turnover is expected to reach 2.0 billion yuan in 1997, he said.
"The company is confident net profit will increase by at least 10 percent in 1997 based on lower production costs," the official said.
"We are pushing hard to boost sales and are launching new products," he said.

The company's board of directors has proposed a 1.31-for-10 bonus issue to B share holders and a 3.5-for-10 bonus issue to A share holders, pending approval of shareholders at a meeting scheduled for April 26.
Meiling offered 100 million B shares at HK$3.07 each in 1996 and listed them on the Shenzhen stock exchange on August 28, last year.
The company said shareholders would also discuss at their meeting a plan to make a three-for-10 rights issue for its A and B shares in 1997, it said in a statement.
Meiling would issue the shares at between 4.5 and 6 yuan and use proceeds to upgrade production technology, it said.
A company official declined to give details.
